title: Source hyper-Ext sequence with a module as target
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $K\in D(A)$ be an object of the ordinary derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $N$ be an $A$-module, and let $u\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $H^a(K)=0$ for every $a>u$. Here $H^a$ denotes standard derived cohomology [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor], $N[0]$ is the complex concentrated in degree zero, and $R\operatorname{Hom}_A$ is the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object site with only the identity covering and coefficient ring $A$. There is an $A$-linear spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence]
$$E_2^{i,j}=\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(H^{-j}(K),N)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad H^{i+j}(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,N[0])),$$
where for $i\geq0$ the Ext group is computed in the abelian category of $A$-modules [def-pc-ext], and $E_2^{i,j}=0$ for $i<0$. The differential $d_s$ has bidegree $(s,1-s)$; $E_{s+1}^{i,j}$ is the kernel of the outgoing differential modulo the image of the incoming differential. Every page is zero outside $i\geq0$, $j\geq-u$, and every fixed bidegree eventually stabilizes to $E_\infty^{i,j}$. For every integer $t$, the abutment $H^t(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,N[0]))$ has a finite exhaustive separated filtration by $A$-submodules [def-sp-filtration] whose successive quotients are the $E_\infty^{t-j,j}$ with $-u\leq j\leq t$; if this interval is empty the abutment is zero. No Noetherian or finite-generation hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0G20, remark-spectral-sequences-ext-variant: renumbered E2 sequence, with M=K and second argument N[0]. Support i>=0, j>=-u and finite filtration are the shifted first-quadrant specialization of its bounded convergence assertion.

proof.text: Choose a representative $M^\bullet$ of $K$ with $M^a=0$ for $a>u$, using the equivalence between cohomological and representative upper bounds in [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Its cohomology is $H^a(K)$. Concretely, for any representative $C^\bullet$, replace it by $\tau_{\leq u}C^\bullet$: the inclusion induces the identity on cohomology in degrees at most $u$ and an isomorphism $0\to H^a(C)=0$ above $u$.

Construct a nonnegative injective resolution $N[0]\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] from [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]. Set $C^0=N$ and, for $r\geq0$, choose an injection $e_r:C^r\hookrightarrow I^r$ into an injective module and set $C^{r+1}=\operatorname{coker}(e_r)$. Define $d_I^r$ as $I^r\twoheadrightarrow C^{r+1}\xrightarrow{e_{r+1}}I^{r+1}$, and set $I^r=0$ for $r<0$. Then $\ker d_I^0=e_0(N)$ and $\ker d_I^r=e_r(C^r)=\operatorname{im}d_I^{r-1}$ for $r>0$, proving that this is the required resolution. This is the elementary recursive construction in Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist (1).

The bounded-below complex of injectives $I^\bullet$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Consequently [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,N[0])$ by the actual Hom complex $T^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(M^\bullet,I^\bullet)$, with the differential of [def-pur-hom-complex]. The one-object identity-covering site identifies module sheaves and their internal Hom with $A$-modules and $\operatorname{Hom}_A$, respectively: the only section and restriction are the module itself and its identity. Thus no comparison with scheme quasi-coherent sheaves is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 070J, lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective; the Hom-complex model in Injectives, Tag 0G1Z, remark-ext-from-filtered-complex

proof.text: Form the first-quadrant double complex [def-sp-double-complex-total] $D^{i,b}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^{u-b},I^i)$ for $i,b\geq0$, zero otherwise. Set $d_I(f)=d_I^i\circ f$ (raising $i$), and $d_{II}(f)=(-1)^{b-u+1}f\circ d_M^{u-b-1}$ (raising $b$). Their squares vanish because $d_M^2=d_I^2=0$, and they commute because precomposition and postcomposition commute and the displayed sign depends only on $b$. In degree $t$, only $-t\leq a\leq u$ can contribute to $T^t=\prod_a\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^a,I^{a+t})$, so this product is a finite direct sum. Writing $a=u-b$ and $i=a+t$ identifies $T^t$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(D)^{t+u}$. The total differential $d_I+(-1)^i d_{II}$ has source-precomposition coefficient $(-1)^{i+b-u+1}=(-1)^{t+1}$, exactly the coefficient $-(-1)^t$ in [def-pur-hom-complex]. Hence this degree translation identifies differentials as well, and $H^t(T)=H^{t+u}(\operatorname{Tot}D)$. This assertion uses degree translation with the same differential, not a convention for signed shift functors.

source.place: Tag 012X, section-double-complex; double complexes, associated total complexes and their two filtrations

proof.text: For fixed $i$, compute the cohomology in $b$ directly from injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Put $a=u-b$, $Z^a=\ker d_M^a$ and $B^a=\operatorname{im}d_M^{a-1}$. A cocycle $f:M^a\to I^i$ kills $B^a$, so restriction induces a map to $\operatorname{Hom}_A(Z^a/B^a,I^i)$. Every map $Z^a/B^a\to I^i$ extends across $Z^a/B^a\hookrightarrow M^a/B^a$, proving surjectivity. A cocycle restricting to zero on $Z^a/B^a$ factors through $M^a/Z^a\cong B^{a+1}$; extending that map across $B^{a+1}\hookrightarrow M^{a+1}$ expresses it as a boundary (up to the invertible sign in $d_{II}$). Therefore $H^b_{II}(D^{i,\bullet})=\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^{u-b}(K),I^i)$. This also covers $b=0$: $M^{u+1}=0$ forces $Z^u=M^u$, so the restriction map has zero kernel. Restriction, quotient factorization and postcomposition commute, so this identification is $A$-linear and compatible with $d_I$.

source.place: Tag 0G20, remark-spectral-sequences-ext-variant; elementary injective-dual cohomology calculation in the module-target double-complex realization

proof.text: Apply the first spectral sequence of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] in the abelian category of $A$-modules (its abelianity is part of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]). Step 5 gives $\widetilde E_1^{i,b}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^{u-b}(K),I^i)$, with differential induced by postcomposition with $d_I$. Hence $\widetilde E_2^{i,b}=H^i\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^{u-b}(K),I^\bullet)$. Since $I^\bullet$ is the K-injective resolution fixed in step 3, [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] identifies this with $H^iR\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^{u-b}(K)[0],N[0])$, and [lem-sc-rhom-cohomology-ext-ring] identifies it with $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(H^{u-b}(K),N)$ for $i\geq0$. These are $A$-linear identifications: the maps send a cocycle to its localized shifted map, and multiplication by $a\in A$ is postcomposition with $a\operatorname{id}_{I^\bullet}$ throughout. All pages and filtration maps are in $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$, so their kernels, images and quotients are $A$-submodules. The spectral-sequence page isomorphisms [def-sp-spectral-sequence] give $\widetilde E_{s+1}=H(\widetilde E_s,d_s)$.

source.place: Tag 0130, lemma-ss-double-complex, first spectral sequence; Injectives Tag 0G20, remark-spectral-sequences-ext-variant

proof.text: Set $E_s^{i,j}=\widetilde E_s^{i,j+u}$ for $s\geq2$. This translation preserves the differential bidegree $(s,1-s)$ and the next-page kernel/image formula. It gives $E_2^{i,j}=\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(H^{-j}(K),N)$, with support $i\geq0$, $j\geq-u$ on every page. By [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences], $\widetilde E_s^{i,b}$ stabilizes, and in degree $n=t+u\geq0$ the first image filtration has $F^0H^n=H^n$, $F^{n+1}H^n=0$ and $\operatorname{gr}^i_FH^n=\widetilde E_\infty^{i,n-i}$. Through step 4 this is a finite exhaustive separated filtration [def-sp-filtration] of $H^tR\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,N[0])$, whose quotients are $E_\infty^{i,t-i}$ for $0\leq i\leq t+u$, equivalently $E_\infty^{t-j,j}$ for $-u\leq j\leq t$. If $t+u<0$, the first-quadrant total complex is zero in that degree, so its cohomology, and thus the abutment, is zero. The construction imposed no condition on $A$ or its modules beyond those in the statement.
